headline: Death toll from attack at Pakistan police HQ rises to 31, including 16 police personnel
summary: An explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in Kohat, Pakistan, has left at least 31 dead and over 100 injured. Fighting with militants is reportedly ongoing.
details: At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and over 100 injured in a militant attack and suicide bombing at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan. Fighting with militants is reportedly still ongoing following the assault.

Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex in Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday afternoon. The complex serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices like the Counter Terrorism Department.

Several militants are believed to be holed up in the Special Branch section of the complex, with an exchange of fire continuing since late Friday night. Their exact number remains unclear, according to a senior police official.

Pakistan attributes the surge in attacks in KP and Balochistan to militancy originating from Afghanistan. The Taliban government in Afghanistan, however, denies any involvement in these cross-border incidents.

These accusations have led to a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighboring countries. Pakistan has previously conducted airstrikes targeting militants on Afghan soil, which Kabul and the UN reported killed dozens of civilians in June.

headline_marked: [[Jamaat-e-Islami warns 8-point demands could become one-point]] if government fails to act
headline: Jamaat-e-Islami warns 8-point demands could become one-point if government fails to act
summary: Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman issued the warning at the start of an 11-party alliance long march from Dhaka to Rangpur, pressing for various national reforms.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman warned today that the 11-party alliance's eight-point demands could escalate into a "one-point" demand if the government fails to address them. He emphasized that such a development would lead to a "very serious situation."

The warning was delivered at the inaugural rally of the Dhaka-Rangpur long march, organized by the alliance to press for their demands. The demands include implementing a referendum verdict, seeking justice for the July massacre, and resolving fuel and fertilizer crises.

Other key demands are controlling essential prices, improving law and order, ending administrative politicization, curbing extortion and corruption, and implementing the Teesta Master Plan. The long march began at 7:00 AM from Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka.

Shafiqur Rahman urged the government to learn from past experiences and accept the people's demands, stating that intimidation would not deter their movement. He asserted that the alliance is advocating for the demands of 180 million people, not just a party agenda.
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam alleged government suppression, citing torn banners and festoons. He also challenged BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman on his future political conduct.

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Ameer Mamunul Haque and Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed reiterated the peaceful and people-oriented nature of the movement, aiming to put the country on the right track.
The long march is scheduled to include five roadside rallies in Gazipur, Tangail, Sirajganj, Bogura, and Gaibandha, culminating in a final rally at Rangpur Zila School ground.

This long march is part of a larger series of protests, following a Dhaka-Chattogram long march earlier this month. Future plans include long marches to Khulna and Sylhet, with a grand rally in Dhaka scheduled for November 14.
